items.title: Scrum Masters — the world needs you now as much as ever
items.excerpt: Image We all know too little planning is ineffective — and I think most of us know too much planning is wasteful in conditions of uncertainty, volatility, and disruptive competition. Bigger, longer, more predictive planning — thus more assumptive, guessworking, and speculative — is ineffective in such conditions, but still the first choice of many organisations. Cognitive traps happen when decisions favor efficiency, control, or comfort over transparency, inspection, and adaptation. Here is one of ten cognitive traps, Increment Misconception: assuming completed parts equal a usable whole ignores the need for integration and meaningful inspection. items.title: How to calculate a ROM estimate and when to use it
items.excerpt: What is a ROM estimate? A rough order of magnitude estimate is used to give you a very high level view of potential project costs. Ideally, you’d be able to provide a definitive estimate, carefully created from loads of input from subject matter experts and plenty of research on past projects and their budgets. But in reality, we rarely have the time or luxury of being able to provide that level of estimate at the earliest stage of project. items.excerpt: When I’m getting ready to leave a job, whether that’s for a holiday or for good, I’ll make sure to do a handover to my boss. That might be as simple as a quick email or a conversation in our last 1:1, but sometimes it’s important to do a bit more than that. I’ve never gone back to a past employer (yet, maybe I will one day), but as 40% of people would consider returning to an employer, it’s worth making sure your exit is smooth, professional, and on good terms.
